deep.reconstruction:
The page has three unrelated blocks. The large block is clearly work on plane gas waves of finite amplitude, the subject of Riemann's 1860 paper.

(A) Top left: Bessel-type integrals.
- Line 1: 2π∫_1^∞ e^{-qt} dt/√(t²−1) = ∫ e^{-qt} log t dt/√(1−t²). The left integral is K_0(q). The right side, presumably over [−1,1] (cf. the fragment '2∫_{-1}^{1}' below), is Riemann trying to express K_0 by an integral over the cut [−1,1] with a logarithmic weight. This is the kind of formula one gets from a contour argument around the branch points ±1. Compare the classical K_0(q) = −(1/π)∫_0^π e^{q cos θ}[γ + log(2q sin²θ)] dθ.
- Line 2: ∫ e^{-qt}(log t − log q) dt/(t√(1−q²/t²)). This is the same type of integral after rescaling t → t/q, since dt/(t√(1−q²/t²)) = dt/√(t²−q²). Splitting off log q is evidently meant to isolate the log q singularity of K_0 at q = 0.
- Neither line is brought to a finished identity.

(B) Middle left: a Gamma-function integral. Riemann writes ∫ e^{θi} Π(μ) dθ/(K+θi)^μ next to ∫_0^∞ e^{-(K+θi)x} (x^{μ−1}) dx. The underlying formula, in Gauss's Π notation (Π(s) = Γ(s+1)), is
  ∫_0^∞ e^{-(K+iθ)x} x^{μ−1} dx = Π(μ−1)/(K+iθ)^μ.
The inverse Fourier integral is then
  ∫_{-∞}^{∞} e^{iθy} dθ/(K+iθ)^μ = 2π y^{μ−1} e^{-Ky}/Π(μ−1) for y > 0, and 0 for y < 0.
This is the device Riemann uses elsewhere (the 1859 zeta paper, Laplace/Fourier inversion).

(C) The rest of the page: isothermal gas dynamics in the hodograph plane.

Set-up (my identification of the variables). Take an isothermal gas with sound speed a and velocity x' = u. Put
  u = 2a(p+q),  log ρ = 2(p−q)  (Riemann writes p−q = log ρ/2).
Then 4ap = u + a log ρ and 4aq = u − a log ρ are Riemann invariants:
- p is constant on the characteristics dx/dt = u+a;
- q is constant on dx/dt = u−a.
Regarding x and t as functions of (p,q), the flow equations become the linear hodograph system
  x_q = a(2(p+q)+1) t_q,  x_p = a(2(p+q)−1) t_p.
Eliminating x gives t_pq = t_p − t_q (my derivation). With t = e^{q−p}T this becomes T_pq + T = 0, a constant-coefficient (Klein–Gordon type) equation.

The particular solution on the page is
  at = sin(p+q) e^{q−p},
  x = (cos(p+q) + 2(p+q) sin(p+q)) e^{q−p}.
Top right, the same solution is written with α = p+q, ρ = q−p:
  at = sin α e^ρ,  x = (cos α + 2α sin α) e^ρ.
It has the potential w = −2cos(p+q) e^{q−p}. Indeed (my check):
- x − (u−a)t = (cos σ + sin σ)e^τ = w_p/2;
- x − (u+a)t = (cos σ − sin σ)e^τ = −w_q/2.

Initial data (t = 0). The condition at = 0 forces p+q = 0, i.e. u = 0 (gas at rest). Then x = e^{q−p}, so q − p = log x, giving q = ½ log x, p = −½ log x and ρ = e^{2(p−q)} = 1/x². The page records the data:
- x < 1: p = q = 0, ρ = 1;
- x > 1: p = −½ log x, q = ½ log x, log ρ/2 = −log x, ρ = 1/(xx).
The density is continuous at x = 1. Riemann then checks at t = 0:
- ∂p/∂x = −1/(2x), ∂q/∂x = 1/(2x);
- a ∂t/∂q = a ∂t/∂p = x (from a t_q = (cos σ + sin σ)e^τ = e^τ = x at σ = 0).

Curves t = const (top right). On these, cot α dα + dρ = 0, i.e. dα = −tan α dρ. Then
  dx = [(sin α + 2α cos α)dα + (cos α + 2α sin α)dρ] e^ρ = (cos²α − sin²α)/cos α · e^ρ dρ = cos 2α/cos α · e^ρ dρ.
So x is monotone along t = const until α = π/4; the page notes p+q = π/4. This marks where the map (p,q) → (x,t) folds, i.e. the onset of multivaluedness and a shock. A line with 2cos α + 2α/sin α is struck out as a slip. Special values:
- α = π/2: at = e^ρ, x = π e^ρ (so x = π·at), and x = π at ρ = 0.

Self-similarity. Dividing the two formulas gives x/(at) = cot σ + 2σ, i.e. x/(at) = cot(x'/2a) + x'/a. So in this solution the velocity depends only on x/t. The side condition sin q e^q < at also appears.

Adjacent simple-wave regions. The constant state p = q = 0 for x < 1 is bordered by simple waves, matched through the potential relations.
- Branch p = 0: 2(x − x't + at) = 2(sin(p+q) + cos(p+q)) e^{q−p}. This gives
  x = at(2q−1) + e^q(sin q + cos q),
  ∂x/∂q|_t = 2at + 2e^q cos q,
  and at q = 0 the boundary characteristic x = 1 − at. The trace x = (cos q + 2q sin q)e^q is also written.
- Branch q = 0: the correct relations (my derivation) are
  x − (u+a)t = (cos p − sin p) e^{−p},
  x = at(2p+1) + (cos p − sin p) e^{−p},
  ∂x/∂p = 2at − 2cos p e^{−p}.
  The boundary characteristic is x = 1 + at; the page writes x > 1 − at.

The next page continues the same problem with shock conditions u(ρ₊ − ρ₋) = x'₊ρ₊ − x'₋ρ₋, x' = 2ap and x − x't + at = φ(p). This confirms the gas-dynamical reading.
errors: Line 1 cannot hold as written. At q → 0 the left side 2π K_0(q) diverges logarithmically, while ∫_{-1}^{1} log|t| dt/√(1−t²) = −π log 2 is finite. Limits, branch of log and constants are missing; it is a tentative step, and line 2 (with log t − log q) is evidently the attempted repair.

Branch q = 0: the page writes x = at(2p+1) + 2(cos p − sin p)e^p and ∂x/∂p = 2at − 2cos p e^p. Consistency with the solution and with the stated derivative requires x = at(2p+1) + (cos p − sin p)e^{−p}, whose derivative is 2at − 2cos p e^{−p}. The factor 2 and the sign of the exponent are slips (or the minus sign is lost in the reading). The left side '(2x − x't − at)' should be 2(x − x't − at).
The struck-out expression (2cos α + 2α/sin α)dρ e^ρ is wrong; Riemann replaced it with the correct cos 2α/cos α · e^ρ dρ.
The fragment 'dx = (+sin α + 2α cos α) − tg α/2 = π/2' is incomplete and garbled, not a valid equation; the corrected line follows it.
The condition written as 'x > 1 − at' for the q = 0 region does not match the boundary characteristic x = 1 + at that follows from the q = 0 formula; the intended inequality is unclear.

results.what: Isothermal gas: Riemann invariants u ± a log ρ (here 4ap, 4aq), with characteristic speeds u ± a
results.modern_name: Riemann invariants / method of characteristics for the 1D Euler equations

results.what: Hodograph linearization x_q = a(2(p+q)+1)t_q, x_p = a(2(p+q)−1)t_p, reducing to t_pq = t_p − t_q, a constant-coefficient linear PDE (T_pq + T = 0 after t = e^{q−p}T)

Explicit exact solution at = sin(p+q)e^{q−p}, x = (cos(p+q)+2(p+q)sin(p+q))e^{q−p}, with potential w = −2cos(p+q)e^{q−p}; it realizes initial data u = 0, ρ = 1/x² (x > 1), ρ = 1 (x < 1), and gives x/(at) = cot(u/2a) + u/a
results.modern_name: Exact isothermal gas-dynamics solution via hodograph (an explicit Riemann-problem-type example)
results.usually_credited_to: unsure (not in the published 1860 paper as far as I know)

results.what: Along t = const, dx = cos2α/cosα · e^ρ dρ, so the map folds at α = p+q = π/4
results.modern_name: Breakdown of the hodograph map / gradient catastrophe, onset of a shock

results.what: Simple-wave regions p = 0 and q = 0 adjoining the constant state, bounded by the characteristics x = 1 ∓ at
results.modern_name: Simple (rarefaction/compression) waves adjacent to a constant state

results.what: Integral representation of 1/(K+iθ)^μ by ∫_0^∞ e^{-(K+iθ)x}x^{μ−1}dx and its Fourier inversion
Attempt to rewrite ∫_1^∞ e^{-qt}dt/√(t²−1) (= K_0(q)) as a log-weighted integral over [−1,1]
results.modern_name: Integral representations / small-argument expansion of the Macdonald function K_0
results.usually_credited_to: Poisson, Kummer, Riemann-era folklore; formal theory Macdonald 1899

deep.surprise_reason: The method (Riemann invariants, hodograph linearization, shock onset) is exactly Riemann's published 1860 work, so it is not surprising in itself. Notable is an unpublished, fully explicit worked example. It is an exact isothermal solution in closed trigonometric-exponential form, matched to concrete initial data (rest state, ρ = 1/x² for x > 1), with the fold of the hodograph map located at p+q = π/4. It also uses the reduction to a constant-coefficient equation. This is a nice unpublished detail but not a new theorem credited to someone later.

transcription_corrections: 'q=0. (2x − x't − at)' should read 'q=0. 2(x − x't − at) = 2(cos p − sin p)e^{(−)p}'.
Top right, 'dx = (+sin α + 2α cos α) − tg α/2 = π/2' is an incomplete scribble. The intended line is dx = ((sin α + 2α cos α)dα + (cos α + 2α sin α)dρ)e^ρ, used with dα = −tg α dρ.
'x = π' beside 'dα = −tg α dρ' most likely belongs to the special case α = π/2 (x = π e^ρ, i.e. x = π at ρ = 0). Cf. the bottom-right 'α = π/2, at = e^ρ, x = π e^ρ'.
In the second integral, 'e^{-[-q-]t}' is an overwritten exponent. The integrand has the form e^{-(q)t}(log t − log q) dt/(t√(1−q²/t²)), with a trailing 'dx' or 'dt' crossed.
'w = −2cos(p+q)e^{q−p}' is correct as read (it is the potential), and the '[?]' can be removed. The variable is the velocity potential-like function w of Riemann 1860, not an unclear symbol.
'p+q = ½, ∂q/∂t = 0' in the middle left is a small marginal scribble, unrelated to the main derivation.

The integrand in '∫ e^{θi} Πμ/(K+θi)^μ ∂θi' presumably carries e^{θ i x} (a dropped variable). The companion line is ∫_0^∞ e^{−(K+θi)x} x^{μ(−1)} dx, with the power of x not legible in the transcription.
